messages:
anya: Quick sync — want to land UX changes for the automatic fallback policy this sprint. Main goals: clearer observability, operator backoff/snooze ergonomics, and a dry-run simulation in the rollout UI. Thoughts?

michael: +1. high level: snooze should be per-route and scoped to an operator action. global snooze feels risky.

sam: Agreed. Also we need structured 'why' breadcrumbs in traces: which signal triggered fallback (latency / err-rate / quota), the threshold, and the evaluation window.

laura: Dry-run in UI would be huge. We can show expected fallback_rate, estimated cost delta, and a simulated sample of requests that would have fallen back. Tiny prototype: a checkbox "simulate changes only" that runs against historical traces.

michael: For operator backoff semantics: we should expose initial backoff, multiplier, and max backoff. Operators sometimes want aggressive backoff for noisy endpoints.

kayla: quick config sketch (for console + API):

```
fallback_policy:
  mode: auto
  triggers:
    - name: 5xx_spike
      metric: error_rate_5xx
      window: 60s
      threshold: 0.05
    - name: high_tail_latency
      metric: p99_latency
      window: 30s
      threshold: 1500ms
  backoff:
    initial: 100ms
    factor: 2
    max: 5s
  snooze:
    enabled: true
    scope: route
    duration: 15m
  audit: true
  dry_run: true
```

kayla: This would be the JSON we persist. Console shows a compact summary and an "advanced" dropdown with raw YAML.

anya: Love it. Two follow-ups: 1) telemetry naming conventions 2) what audit logs keep when snoozed/dry-run.

michael: Telemetry: publish these time-series: fallback_rate, fallback_reason_{name}, fallback_trigger_window, operator_snooze_count, simulated_fallback_rate. Also emit event payloads into the trace for each decision with ids.

sam: Audit logs: always record decisions, even if snoozed, but mark them "operator-snoozed". For dry-run, record simulated_decision=true. Retention: 90 days by default; make it configurable per org.

laura: UI ideas: a compact timeline in the rollout page showing windows where automatic fallback would have fired, with hover details (traffic, metric value, matched trigger). Clicking a window opens the sample requests.

michael: Important: we need a cheap sampling mode for request snapshots (1/1000 by default) to avoid storage blowup. Make sample rate adjustable.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: fallback-ui/proto branch merged to staging — e2e tests queued.

kayla: UX edgecase: operator clicks snooze but later realizes they need to escalate. We should include a clear "undo" in operator inbox + an audit entry with operator id and reason.

anya: Good. Also want a simple admin override that disables auto-fallback globally for a short window (for infra ops) but preserves audit. Should be gated behind role perms.

michael: For API semantics: PATCH /routes/:id/fallback_policy should support a query param ?dry_run=true that returns simulation results without mutating. Also POST /rollouts/:id/simulate that runs longer simulations asynchronously and returns artifact link.

sam: For telemetry schema, let's standardize tag keys: route_id, model_variant, region, customer_tier. Include opt-in PII scrubbing for any sampled request body.

laura: UX copy: avoid "failover" verb in public console. Use "fallback" or "degrade". Add short tooltip definitions.

anya: Next steps: kayla to prototype the UI panel + simulate button, michael to draft API changes, sam to write telemetry spec, laura to mock timeline. I'll open a PR with acceptance criteria and link design mocks.

michael: I'll also add an alerting guideline in the doc: if simulated_fallback_rate > 5% for production traffic, warn and require explicit confirmation.

kayla: Will start prototype today, aiming for demo on Thursday.

ops-bot: reminder-bot: weekly-sync in #eng-platform scheduled Thu 11:00 for fallback UX demo.

anya: thanks all. I'll file the RFC and tag folks. :thumbsup:

laura: Nice, thanks.

michael: LGTM

sam: SGTM

ok: I'll paste the proto link after lunch. :)
